sentences.text: Adult Sonorasaurus was a massive creature estimated to weigh around 16 tons, measure approximately 15 meters in length, and stand 8 meters tall.
The name Sonorasaurus means "Sonora lizard" and refers to the Sonora River in the Sonoran Desert where the fossils were found.
Sonorasaurus was declared the official state dinosaur of Arizona on April 10, 2018, following a petition by an 11-year-old student.
Fossils were discovered in November 1994 by student Richard Thompson in the Turney Ranch Formation of the Whetstone Mountains in southern Arizona.
Ratkevich initially classified Sonorasaurus as a member of the Brachiosauridae family.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Sonorasaurus as Brachiosauridae.
Sonorasaurus lived during the Early to Late Cretaceous, approximately 112 to 93 million years ago.
Phylogenetic studies have failed to reach a consensus on whether Sonorasaurus belongs within the Brachiosauridae or outside of it.
